what_worked: Strong thesis sustained across every slide with a memorable gold-rush metaphor and clean visual hierarchy.
fix_next: Median values are systematically wrong (Education $2,142 vs. $2,435; AI $446 vs. $503); verify all numbers against the actual dataset before presenting.
verdict: Compelling narrative undermined by pervasive median-revenue errors and an unsourced exit-multiple claim.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3/4/5: Education median shown as $2,142 (actual $2,435); AI median $446 (actual $503); Marketing $1,586 (actual $2,369.50); Analytics $1,294 (actual $419); E-comm $155 (actual $387). Multiple other category medians also diverge materially. Slide 7: 3.15x AI exit multiple and 2.3x market median appear fabricated—no revenue-multiple field exists in the frozen dataset. Slide 2: 'Fintech' listed as a category with 16 companies but does not appear in the reference category list. Slide 4: '5x the median revenue' claim based on wrong medians (actual ratio ~4.8x, minor but built on wrong inputs).

evidence.insight: The core insight—AI is the most crowded category yet mid-pack in median revenue—is genuinely interesting and decision-useful. The AI-vs-Education comparison (slide 4) and the growth-rate parity observation (slide 6) add layers. However, the exit-multiple argument (slide 7) would be the strongest insight if it were verifiable, but it appears unsourced from the dataset.
evidence.narrative: Excellent arc: title question → crowding → yield → head-to-head → ranking → momentum → valuation → verdict → recommendations. Each slide builds on the prior one. The gold-rush metaphor is sustained without becoming forced. The landing on slide 8 synthesizes cleanly.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets up the question well. Slide 9 cites source and n=1,000/726 categorized, which is good. However, 274 missing categories and 241 missing countries are never discussed as limitations. The audience is implicitly founders/buyers/analysts (slide 9) but this isn't established until the end. No mention of the 216 zero-revenue companies across the full dataset or how missingness might bias category medians.
evidence.accuracy: Systematic median errors across nearly every category shown (slides 3-5). Education off by ~$293, Marketing off by ~$783, Analytics off by ~$875, AI off by ~$57, E-comm off by ~$232. The exit-multiple figures (3.15x, 2.3x, 1.2x on slide 7) have no apparent basis in the frozen dataset—the dataset contains revenue multiples but the reference B2B/B2C medians are 2.35x/2.30x, not category-specific multiples as presented. Fintech appears as a 13th category not in the reference list. The 27% claim on slide 2 (197/726 ≈ 27.1%) is correct.
evidence.visual: Consistently excellent design system: warm palette, gold-rush theming, clear hierarchy with section labels, restrained use of color to highlight AI. Bubble chart (slide 2) is effective. Nugget sizing (slide 3) is creative. The balance/seesaw on slide 7 is visually appealing. Typography is strong throughout. Minor issue: slide 6's large circles are somewhat decorative for just two numbers.
evidence.ai_slop: none—the metaphor is sustained and specific, not generic filler. Design is cohesive and purposeful.
